newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE - HONOURS EVEN AS FEYENOORD, AJAX CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE - HONOURS EVEN AS FEYENOORD, AJAX CLASH.

text.p: Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam shared the spoils in a highly-charged Dutch first division encounter on Sunday.
Three penalties in the first 15 minutes set the scene for an electrifying match, marred earlier by fighting between fans and police in Rotterdam and the stoning of the Ajax team coach.

Ajax, desperate to end a slump that has pitched them in mid-table and facing an early exit from the European Cup, missed the chance to get off to a dream start, when Patrick Kluivert blasted his spot-kick over the bar after Nigerian winger Tijani Babangida was pulled back in the area in the second minute.
Two minutes later, Feyenoord veteran Ronald Koeman showed him how it should be done, converting a penalty after Winston Bogarde bundled over Feyenoord's Swedish striker Henryk Larsson.
On 15 minutes, Geoffrey Claes handled in the Feyenoord area. Ronald de Boer stepped up to make it 1-1 with a fiercely-struck penalty.
But within a minute Bernard Schuiteman had restored the home side's lead, heading home the rebound after Koeman's free-kick had crashed against Edwin van der Sar's bar.
Kluivert, the second-minute sinner, turned saviour midway through the second half, when he punished the Feyenoord defence, slotting home after a neat one-two with Nordin Wooter.

Ajax coach Louis van Gaal, missing half his first team through injury, opted to play Mario Melchiot at the heart of the defence with Arno Splinter and Winston Bogarde guarding against incursions from Feyenoord's wide-men.

Ajax, facing a bleak mid-winter break -- out of contention for a 27th domestic title and clinging to hopes of a continued presence in Europe -- enjoyed more of the possession in the first half, but failed to capitalise, as Feyenoord, employing a five-man defence, snuffed out most attacks.
The fixture, which has never ended goalless, was played out in freezing temperatures, but the entertainment level was enough to keep most fans warm.
Leading 2-1 in the second half, Feyenoord sat back to try and soak up Ajax pressure, but paid the penalty when Kluivert and Wooter weaved their pretty patterns in the area.
Ajax almost clinched the three points late in the game when Koeman's mis-directed header from a Marc Overmars cross almost beat his own keeper Ed de Goey.

The result, which ended a run of five Ajax league victories in Rotterdam, gives PSV Eindhoven, 2-0 winners at AZ Alkmaar, a three-point lead over Feyenoord at the top of the table. Ajax are fifth, eight points adrift of their Rotterdam rivals.

The game, one of the classics in the Dutch soccer calendar, was brought forward from an evening kick-off so that police could control fans during daylight hours, but there was violence before the game and kick-off was delayed by 15 minutes.
Feyenoord fans lobbed a fire-bomb at police in the centre of Rotterdam and Ajax fans arriving by train pelted police with ball-bearings. Mounted police charged supporters, making 17 arrests.
Nearer the ground, Feyenoord fans attacked Ajax's team coach, throwing stones, bottles and sticks, breaking one window and nearly injuring Ajax defender Menno Willems.
Bram Peper, mayor of Rotterdam, earlier gave police special powers to arrest anyone making their way to the ground without a valid ticket and who was seen as a threat to public safety.
Van Gaal said he was unhappy with security measures around the stadium, but admitted that the attack on his team bus had sent his players out on to the pitch in aggressive mood.
Teams:

Feyenoord: 1-Ed de Goey, 2-Henk Fraser (12-Clemens Zwijnenberg 28), 4-Ronald Koeman, 5-Bernard Schuiteman, 6-Geoffrey Claes, 3-Patricio Graff; 7-Kees van Wonderen, 9-Pablo Sanchez (15-Henk Vos 69), 11-Giovanni van Brockhorst; 8-Gaston Taument (14-Marek Saganowski 79), 10-Henryk Larsson.

Ajax: 1-Edwin van der Sar, 4-Arno Splinter, 2-Arnold Scholten, 3-Mario Melchiot, 5-Winston Bogarde (18-John Veldman 46); 6-Ronald de Boer, 10-Nordin Wooter, 8-Kiki Musampa; 7-Tijjani Babangida (15-Ivan Gabrich 75), 9-Patrick Kluivert, 11-Marc Overmars (14-Martijn Reuser 86)
